# wend

> Symbolic, typed, invertible filesystem paths built from Python t-strings (3.14+).

wend is a Python 3.14 library that builds filesystem paths as symbolic expressions from
t-strings (PEP 750). One expression renders paths from values (`render`), reads values back
out of a path (`match`) and finds the existing paths it describes (`glob`); it also carries
conditions, relations to other paths, schemas, inference and lineage. Install with
`pip install wend`. Each link below is the Markdown version of a page of
https://lmmx.github.io/wend/.

## Start here

- [Home](<https://lmmx.github.io/wend/pr-preview/pr-110/index.md>): Symbolic, typed, invertible filesystem paths built from Python t-strings (3.14+).

## Get started

- [Installation](<https://lmmx.github.io/wend/pr-preview/pr-110/getting-started/installation/index.md>): Install wend with pip or uv: it needs Python 3.14 or later, has no dependencies, and has three optional extras.
- [Quickstart](<https://lmmx.github.io/wend/pr-preview/pr-110/getting-started/quickstart/index.md>): Build a path expression, render it, match a path back to its values, find files with glob, and check a condition, in about ten minutes.

## Concepts

- [How wend works](<https://lmmx.github.io/wend/pr-preview/pr-110/concepts/index.md>): The idea behind wend: an expression describes a path, and every feature is something done with that description.
- [Expressions](<https://lmmx.github.io/wend/pr-preview/pr-110/concepts/expressions/index.md>): What a path expression records, and how P, T and / build one from literal text, parameters and t-strings.
- [Parameters](<https://lmmx.github.io/wend/pr-preview/pr-110/concepts/parameters/index.md>): The four kinds of parameter, the type, choices and default a parameter declares, and why a value bound to a segment parameter cannot traverse.
- [Operations](<https://lmmx.github.io/wend/pr-preview/pr-110/concepts/operations/index.md>): Path operations on expressions: which are computed from structure, which wait for bindings, and which are rejected when the expression is built.
- [Rendering and matching](<https://lmmx.github.io/wend/pr-preview/pr-110/concepts/matching/index.md>): The two directions of an expression: render paths from bindings, and match paths back to verified, typed bindings.
- [Relations](<https://lmmx.github.io/wend/pr-preview/pr-110/concepts/relations/index.md>): How an expression keeps the paths it was built from: base, base_rel, child, sibling, cousin, rebase and under.
- [Effects](<https://lmmx.github.io/wend/pr-preview/pr-110/concepts/effects/index.md>): Which operations touch the filesystem, how conditions declare what a path must be when it is used, and what the checks do and do not guarantee.

## Guides

- [Datasets and shards](<https://lmmx.github.io/wend/pr-preview/pr-110/guides/datasets/index.md>): Declare a sharded dataset's layout once, render every shard path in bulk, list the shards that exist with glob, and find the missing ones.
- [Pipeline steps](<https://lmmx.github.io/wend/pr-preview/pr-110/guides/pipelines/index.md>): Declare what a pipeline step reads and writes with requires and ensures, run it as a Step, and see what a second run and a failed run do.
- [Mapping between trees](<https://lmmx.github.io/wend/pr-preview/pr-110/guides/lenses/index.md>): Map source paths to output paths and back with a Lens, find the outputs that are stale or orphaned, and see why a lossless lens refuses two sources for one target.
- [Untrusted input](<https://lmmx.github.io/wend/pr-preview/pr-110/guides/untrusted-input/index.md>): Build paths from values that come from outside the program: bind them to segment and SubPath parameters, keep path parameters under a base with Under, and know what the checks do not protect.
- [Lineage and caching](<https://lmmx.github.io/wend/pr-preview/pr-110/guides/lineage/index.md>): Explain how a path expression was derived, record which files each pipeline step made from which with a Ledger, find what is stale, and name cache entries after their inputs with content_key.
- [Settings and anchors](<https://lmmx.github.io/wend/pr-preview/pr-110/guides/settings/index.md>): Declare an application's paths once with defaults, bind them from a settings object such as a dataclass, a Pydantic model or a named tuple, override with keywords, and start paths from the home, working and XDG directories.

## Integrations

- [Pydantic](<https://lmmx.github.io/wend/pr-preview/pr-110/integrations/pydantic/index.md>): Validate the path fields of a Pydantic model against a wend expression with PathOf: accept a path or its bindings, get a Match back, use conditions as validators, and read the errors.
- [Polars](<https://lmmx.github.io/wend/pr-preview/pr-110/integrations/polars/index.md>): Render an expression for every row of a Polars DataFrame with resolve_frame: what it validates, what it lowers to Polars, what it refuses, and the fallback with compile().many.

## API reference

- [API reference](<https://lmmx.github.io/wend/pr-preview/pr-110/reference/index.md>): wend's public API, module by module, generated from the docstrings.
- [wend](<https://lmmx.github.io/wend/pr-preview/pr-110/reference/api/wend/index.md>): The wend package: building, resolving, matching and discovering path expressions.
- [wend.anchors](<https://lmmx.github.io/wend/pr-preview/pr-110/reference/api/anchors/index.md>): Anchors: the home directory, the working directory and the XDG base directories.
- [wend.conditions](<https://lmmx.github.io/wend/pr-preview/pr-110/reference/api/conditions/index.md>): Conditions a path must meet when it is realised, and their effects.
- [wend.errors](<https://lmmx.github.io/wend/pr-preview/pr-110/reference/api/errors/index.md>): The exceptions wend raises, all subclasses of WendError.
- [wend.fs](<https://lmmx.github.io/wend/pr-preview/pr-110/reference/api/fs/index.md>): The filesystem protocol that glob and infer use, with local and fsspec backends.
- [wend.infer](<https://lmmx.github.io/wend/pr-preview/pr-110/reference/api/infer/index.md>): Infer path expressions from an existing directory tree.
- [wend.schema](<https://lmmx.github.io/wend/pr-preview/pr-110/reference/api/schema/index.md>): Declare a directory layout as a schema of files and directories, and check trees against it.
- [wend.lineage](<https://lmmx.github.io/wend/pr-preview/pr-110/reference/api/lineage/index.md>): Lineage of expressions and of the files made from them.
- [wend.query](<https://lmmx.github.io/wend/pr-preview/pr-110/reference/api/query/index.md>): Queries over discovered paths, with filesystem predicates.
- [wend.templates](<https://lmmx.github.io/wend/pr-preview/pr-110/reference/api/templates/index.md>): Ready-made path templates, such as numbered shards.
- [wend.frame](<https://lmmx.github.io/wend/pr-preview/pr-110/reference/api/frame/index.md>): Vectorised resolution and matching of path columns with Polars.
- [wend.pydantic](<https://lmmx.github.io/wend/pr-preview/pr-110/reference/api/pydantic/index.md>): Path fields for Pydantic models.

## Background

- [Future Paths and wend](<https://lmmx.github.io/wend/pr-preview/pr-110/background/future-paths/index.md>): How the five Future Paths essays map onto wend: what was built, what changed on the way, and what is still open.

## Optional

- [Development](<https://lmmx.github.io/wend/pr-preview/pr-110/maintainers/development/index.md>): The repository's layout, how to set up and test wend, the semantic contract and the tests that check it, and the conventions for commits and journal entries.
- [Releasing](<https://lmmx.github.io/wend/pr-preview/pr-110/maintainers/releasing/index.md>): How a wend release is made: the Deploy Release workflow bumps the version and tags it, and CI publishes the package to PyPI with Trusted Publishing.
- [Project history](<https://lmmx.github.io/wend/pr-preview/pr-110/background/history/index.md>): wend's development journal: how the dated entries are written and labelled, what each one records, and where to start reading.
- [Documentation](<https://lmmx.github.io/wend/pr-preview/pr-110/maintainers/documentation/index.md>): How wend's documentation site is built, checked, tested and published to GitHub Pages.
